newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - Hong Kong newspaper headlines - Mar 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Hong Kong newspaper headlines - Mar 24.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- APPLE DAILY -- The Democratic Party's Szeto Wah said members of the party would not leave Hong Kong after the handover for fear of not being allowed to come back. He said the party would stay in Hong Kong and continue to fight for democracy and freedom despite its worries over the territory's political future.
-- TA KUNG PAO -- People in Hong Kong and China organised all kinds of activities at the weekend -- including parades and lion dances -- to mark the 100-day countdown to the handover on June 30.
-- WEN WEI PO -- The head of China's Planning Committee, Chen Jinhua, said the country had effectively controlled inflation while maintaining rapid economic growth.
-- MING PAO -- Experts warned that speculation in property, taxi licences, stamps and even watches and running shoes would weaken Hong Kong's economic competitiveness.
-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- Governor Chris Patten urged future Chief Executive Tung Chee-hwa to govern Hong Kong with a light touch and not to copy the way Singapore is ruled.
-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- The World Bank warned that the record amounts of capital that flood into China every year are likely to begin slowing as investment conditions on the mainland change.

-- Sources said Hong Kong had lost out to Tokyo as the site of the International Monetary Fund's proposed Asian headquarters but that the territory was still likely to secure an IMF role in the region.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- A top Taiwan official said the island would demand recognition from Beijing in its dealings with Hong Kong after the handover.
